newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel worried by possible U.S.-Saudi F-16 deal.
newsitem.headline: Israel worried by possible U.S.-Saudi F-16 deal.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu expressed concern on Wednesday about a possible U.S. deal to sell F-16 fighter aircraft to Saudi Arabia.

"We view this with severity. Arming Saudi Arabia with 100 advanced planes and advanced weaponry is a violation of the strategic balance in the Middle East," Israel's Itim news agency quoted Netanyahu as telling reporters aboard his plane en route to Washington for a state visit.
Netanyahu told reporters he would raise the issue of arms sales to Saudi Arabia with U.S. administration officials during his three-day visit.
The United States said last month Saudi Arabia was shopping for jet fighters, but reacted cautiously to a report it would buy up to 100 Lockheed Martin Corp F-16s in a multibillion-dollar deal.
A U.S. Defence Department spokesman said the Saudis were seeking replacements for their ageing fleet of 114 F-5 fighters bought from the United States.

Saudi Defence and Aviation Minister Prince Sultan, due in Washington later this month to meet U.S. Defence Secretary William Cohen, denied on Tuesday his trip was intended to clinch a military aircraft deal but admitted the kingdom was looking for a replacement for its F-5s.
Israel and Saudi Arabia, which do not have diplomatic ties, are key U.S. allies.
